title: Judging and Grading every Fitness Channel (V: Renaissance Periodization, The Bioneer...)
summary: Part five of NH's series grading fitness channels on 20 criteria out of 20 each. Scores: Brian Alsruhe 138, Jeremy Ethier 107, The Bioneer 149, Bald Omni Man 144, Renaissance Periodization 148. Along the way he states his views on drug transparency, supplement sponsorships, science-washing, clickbait and fanboy culture.
claims: Brian Alsruhe's simple strongman-based programming (giant sets) gives better muscle gains than many bodybuilders' advice; you do not need complicated programs
Alsruhe's dislike of isolation is preference, not logic; strongman carries will not fully build arms or traps
Alsruhe made strongman accessible to ordinary people of every age and size, and gets little credit for it
Enhanced creators who never discuss their drug use do less harm than those who promote it, because promotion creates new users
Taking money from a supplement company costs a creator points even if the company is good
Creators who prioritise YouTube over their own training run out of real knowledge, because knowledge comes from practice
Jeremy Ethier's novice-oriented content becomes useless after six months to a year of lifting and leads to plateaus
Taking advice from someone who never got big themselves tends to keep you small
Putting science in titles while citing studies without cross-checking is prostituting science
Thumbnails with a photoshopped bigger arm misrepresent your actual results
Correcting posture requires strengthening the musculature and practising active standing; there is no quick fix
The Bioneer's functional fitness is the most useful content for the sedentary majority because it needs no equipment
Functional fitness is an entry point; most people will eventually want to specialise
Promoting nootropics to an uneducated audience is selling smart pills and is risky
Bald Omni Man gives skinny beginners the right basics: bulk, gain weight, stop guarding your six-pack, get stronger on compounds
There is no such thing as a dangerous lift; it depends on how you perform it
Rejecting the idea of a hard natural limit and over-complicated theories is the most anti-blackpill message in fitness
Mike Israetel/RP deserve top marks for programming and credentials (PhD, Temple University teaching, US Olympic work)
Programming is the most important thing for natural lifters
Intelligent people build mental systems they cannot see outside of; Israetel argues to win, not to find truth
RP's enhanced crew and before/after-drug transformation videos blackpill naturals by suggesting drugs are needed
Promoting oral steroids to an audience that includes teenagers is irresponsible
Calling Israetel Dr. Mike unprompted marks a fanboy; following a smart person does not make you smart unless you apply the concepts
Videos of about 10-20 minutes hit the sweet spot for conciseness
